input.assertion: For every parsed command, the parser returns the declared command record or a deterministic error

subject.kind: A parser function in the product source that turns one command line into a record
subject.verdict: Given the same command line it always returns the same record or the same error value, so a program compares each return value with the declared record and fails on any mismatch

input.assertion: A fresh CLI session exposes every canonical role installed in its native registry

subject.verdict: A schema-constrained LLM response only lists existing registry names; a test compares the returned name set with independently enumerated installed definitions. No model judgment decides availability or the verdict.

input.assertion: A CLI recommends the most suitable installed role for each task description

subject.verdict: An LLM interprets each task and selects a role; fixed cases deterministically grade the returned JSON recommendation

input.assertion: The routing skill selects the evidence specialist for each assertion

subject.kind: Markdown instructions that a language model follows when a user invokes them
subject.verdict: On each run the model reads one assertion, decides which specialist fits it, and answers with one JSON object; a script compares that object's fields with expected values recorded for a set of sample assertions

input.assertion: The architecture keeps evidence-specialist dependencies acyclic

subject.kind: Design intent spread across free-form Markdown skill instructions that name one another in prose; no import graph, manifest, or call table records which skill hands work to which
subject.verdict: Nothing executes and nothing emits output to compare against; a reviewer settles it only by reading every skill and judging whether any hand-off leads back to the skill that made the call
